description: Issue #839 AC1, with CASE as the discriminating variable: `define tally` then `define TALLY`. OpenLogo identifiers are case-insensitive with a lowercase canonical, so these are one name and the second declaration is a duplicate — a case-SENSITIVE registration would accept the program and print `2`. Two further properties are pinned that an all-lowercase fixture cannot see: `params.name` carries the SURFACE spelling of the LATER declaration (`TALLY`, exactly as written, not folded), while `params.original_span` points at the earlier one, so the message can name the line the learner already used without claiming they spelled it the same way.
